round1_to_round2.independence_of_convergence: Mostly anchoring, with some independent checking. Four agents (2, 3, 4 and 5) adopted my round-1 17.6x median and my SPOT conversion at about 1.17 without changing them. Four agents (2, 3, 4 and 5) used my $3.5B net cash at the horizon. agent_3 copied my erroneous taxed CY27 adjusted EPS ($8.12, against my ~$8.2) and NTM EPS ($9.65). The fair values cluster at $158-174 because the agents share one multiple and one method, so this is not five independent confirmations. Some checking was independent: agents 2, 4 and 5 found that my $8.2 taxed EPS implied about a 16% tax rate, agent_1 found the EUR/USD error, agent_5 found the 13 Aug announcement date, and agent_3 raised the SBC-basis point. Each of those corrected me, which suggests they did not just copy. Treat the round-2 cluster as one well-checked view, not as five.

disagreements.topic: Taxed CY2027 adjusted EPS (my round-1 ~$8.2 against $7.56-7.75)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor: about $8.2, copied by agent_3 ($8.12). agent_2 $7.85 (20%). agent_4 $7.66 (21%). agent_5 $7.75. agent_1 $8.15 on its own above-consensus EBITDA build, and it notes that my figure mixed conventions.
disagreements.resolution: The agents are right, and my round-1 figure was an error. $9.69 x 207M = $2.01B of nearly untaxed adjusted pretax income. Taxed at 21-22% that is $7.56-7.66 a share. My $8.2 taxed only the GAAP pretax (that is, it treated the SBC add-back as tax-free), which is an implied tax rate of about 15.5% on adjusted pretax income. Peers' non-GAAP EPS adds back SBC net of tax, so the comparable figure is about $7.66 (21%). The same error affected my taxed GAAP CY27 figure: it is $5.57 ($7.07/0.99 x 0.785), not $5.9 (agent_3 is right). CY28 ($10.10 adjusted, $7.60 GAAP) was taxed correctly. Corrected NTM at Oct-2027: about $9.49 adjusted ($9.65 before) and about $7.10 GAAP. Implication: RDDT trades at 19.8x taxed CY27 adjusted EPS, not 18.5x.
disagreements.evidence: Q2'26 press release: H1 pretax $462.6M, tax $5.7M, net income $456.8M; StockAnalysis CY27 non-GAAP $9.69; arithmetic shown.

disagreements.topic: SBC basis of the peer median (agent_3: SBC-expensed peers about 22x against SBC-adding peers about 12x)
disagreements.positions: agent_3 argues that the blended 17.6x median flatters RDDT because RDDT's SBC (about 12% of revenue) is among the highest in the set, and it gives a GAAP-basis method equal weight. The other agents apply 17.5-18.2x to taxed adjusted EPS.
disagreements.resolution: Half right. The round-1 median was not on one basis. META, GOOGL, NFLX and SPOT consensus expenses SBC, while PINS, SNAP, APP, TTD, DUOL, ROKU and MTCH add it back. But the 22x-versus-12x split is mostly a quality and growth confound (the SBC-adding group holds the de-rated PINS, SNAP, TTD and MTCH), not an accounting effect. Converting every peer to one basis using reported SBC (XBRL, H1'26 annualized, after tax at 21%) gives these medians. SBC-expensed: META 21.3, GOOGL 23.0, NFLX 17.6, SPOT 27.9, PINS 23.5, SNAP 19.4, APP 14.0, TTD 45, DUOL 27.4, for a median of about 23.0x. SBC-added-back: META 17.2, GOOGL 20.4, NFLX about 17.4, SPOT about 26, PINS 8.2, SNAP 7.3, APP 13.5, TTD 12.0, DUOL 19.2, for a median of about 17.2x. I pick SBC-expensed (GAAP-equivalent) as the primary basis because SBC is a real cost and RDDT's is high. At about 23x on taxed GAAP NTM of $7.10 that is $163, and the adjusted cross-check of 17.2x x $9.49 is $163. Both bases agree once they are consistent. agent_3's 22x on GAAP plus 17.6x on adjusted is close; its 12x subgroup argument should not be used on its own.
disagreements.evidence: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (FY2025 and H1'26) and diluted shares (Q2'26) for PINS ($556M H1, 562.9M), SNAP ($513M, 1,663M), TTD ($219M, 470M), DUOL ($73M, 50.0M), META ($13.69B, 2,566M), GOOGL ($14.71B), APP ($169M), RDDT ($169M); StockAnalysis CY27 EPS from comps_review. disagreements.resolution: Reconciled at $162. Consistent-basis P/E: $163 (GAAP) and $163 (adjusted). summary: Round 2 converged at $158-174, but the convergence is mostly anchoring on my round-1 inputs, three of which the agents themselves showed were wrong: the taxed CY27 EPS (about $7.66, not $8.2), EUR/USD (1.121, not 1.17) and the S&P announcement date (13 Aug). On one consistent SBC basis (23x GAAP-equivalent or 17.2x adjusted) RDDT already trades at a 15-18% premium to peers. That premium is not justified as persistent, given Google traffic and licence risk. Applying the median to taxed NTM EPS, plus about $4.0B of net cash, gives $162 (+7%). With 55-70% volatility and an unconfirmed Q3 print (29 Oct or 4 Nov), the ladder stays within about 1pp of the forecasters' mean.
